name: Simples Vet
tagline: Cloud practice management for veterinary clinics: patient records, appointments, prescriptions, inventory and billing.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible part of this, a table of pets, their owners, and a calendar of appointments, is genuinely a weekend build and an agent will nail it. The part that keeps clinics paying is everything downstream of the appointment: Brazilian fiscal invoicing, prescription and controlled-substance records that have to survive a CRMV inspection, stock movements tied to each procedure, cash drawer closing, and a receptionist who is not the person who wrote the code. A one-person build also quietly assumes one person: real clinics have three vets, two receptionists, a groomer, and role permissions that matter when someone deletes a record. And when the invoicing integration breaks on a Friday, a self-hosted app has no support line. Build the records app if you want a personal pet health log; do not build it as a clinic replacement.
coreLoopDIY: A local pet and owner registry with visit history, vaccine and deworming reminders, and printable consultation notes.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to run it on
Encrypted backups if any real animal records go in
A printer or PDF export for prescriptions and notes
whatYouLose: Brazilian fiscal document issuance (NFS-e and friends) and the certificate plumbing behind it
Prescription and controlled-substance records formatted the way regulators expect
Inventory that decrements when a procedure consumes it, plus purchase and cost tracking
Multi-user roles, so reception, vets and management all share one unaudited login
Someone to call when billing or reminders break during clinic hours
moatNotes: Vertical SaaS in a regulated market: the schema is easy, the paperwork it produces is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: A vet clinic is not buying a database, it is buying the ability to hand a client a legal invoice, print a prescription that holds up, know how much ketamine is on the shelf, and close the register at the end of the day with numbers that match. All of that is country-specific, inspection-facing work that changes when the rules change, and the vendor absorbs that change. Add years of accumulated patient history that nobody is going to re-key, and the switching cost alone outlasts any enthusiasm for self-hosting.
notes: The pet registry is a weekend; the invoice the clinic hands the client is not. The moat is fiscal and veterinary compliance in one specific country, maintained by someone else.
prompt:
Build a local-first veterinary records app for a single practitioner. This is a personal patient log, not a clinic management system.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/vet.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth, no cloud, no telemetry

Data model:
- owners: name, phone, email, address, notes
- patients: name, species, breed, sex, birthdate, microchip, weight history, owner_id, allergies, notes, photo path
- visits: patient_id, date, reason, exam findings, diagnosis, treatment, weight at visit, free-text notes
- prescriptions: visit_id, drug, dose, route, frequency, duration, instructions
- reminders: patient_id, type (vaccine, deworming, recheck), due_date, done_at

Features that must work:
- Owner and patient CRUD with search by patient name, owner name, or phone
- Patient page showing full visit timeline, weight chart, active reminders
- New visit form that can attach prescriptions and auto-create a follow-up reminder
- Printable A4 view for a consultation summary and for a prescription, via browser print CSS
- Dashboard listing reminders due in the next 30 days and overdue ones
- Export everything to JSON and CSV from a settings page; nightly file copy of vet.db into ./data/backups

Explicitly out of scope: invoicing, fiscal documents, tax integration, payments, inventory, staff roles, multi-tenant, SMS or WhatsApp sending, mobile app.

Seed the database with 8 fake patients across 5 owners so the UI is not empty on first run. Put nothing in .env except an optional DATA_DIR override. Write a README with setup, backup, and a blunt line stating this is not a compliant clinical or fiscal record system.
